Static stat critDamagePct with NO durationSec/durationShots ('continuously'), target self. Behavioural: >=1 self apply of value 6.61 (RED if the line was dropped as an unreachable HP gate) and zeroing it must reduce the total. Static stat critRatePct (unscoped in the text, so NOT critRateNormalPct), durationSec 10, target self, trigger burstCast (or the equivalent fullBurstEnter + ownBurstGate:'cast'). Behavioural: apply count >=1 (RED if dropped as an unreachable HP gate) and exactly equal to her burst-slot damage-hit count; team fullBurstStart count >= that; and when FB starts exceed her casts (helm the co-B3 takes rotations) the fullBurstEnter patch must apply strictly more often — RED on a bare fullBurstEnter or a passive encoding. durationSec 40 must out-damage faithful (window really lapses); zeroing must under-damage; teammates inert.

Static kind flatDamage atkPct 849.15, trigger burstCast, target enemy, core not set (no 'core strike' wording). Event-level: every srcSlot 'burst' hit has fbMajorApplied false (a cast lands pre-FB window) and rangeApplied false (riders force no-range); exactly one hit per cast (single boss, not per-target fan-out). Halving atkPct must reduce scarlet's total and leave every teammate byte-identical.
unmodeled/note JSON contains '4.01' and '138.24'; no effect anywhere has kind 'ignored' (validator rule); all three slot arrays declared.

fixtures: controlComp('scarlet', true) for all 11 runs — liter (B1) + crown (B2) so the Burst III chain actually completes (a lone B3 makes ZERO Full Bursts and every burst assertion would be vacuous), and helm deliberately KEPT as a second Burst III: team Full Bursts then outnumber scarlet's own casts, which is the only way the burstCast-vs-fullBurstEnter counterfactual can discriminate. helm's ally buffs (incl. critRateNormalPct) are harmless because every claim is a same-fixture A/B on totals or an event-count identity. Deterministic (no seed). Boss is Fire and scarlet's kit carries no elemental-advantage line, so nothing depends on the element matchup. All counterfactuals are located by predicate (stat + magnitude) via a shape-agnostic slot reader that accepts either slot -> Block[] or slot -> {blocks: Block[]}, so the file is blind to block ordering and to which of the two documented OverrideFile shapes the harness returns; a missing kit line surfaces as a named throw inside the patch, i.e. a MISSING failure with a readable message.
gaps: skill1 'Current HP ▼ 4.01%' — it.skip: no HP-pool primitive (immortal boss, no unit HP, no consumer). Load-bearing only as the mechanism behind the two HP gates.

skill2 '30% chance of activating when attacked / 138.24% of final ATK' — it.skip: no on-attacked trigger in the schema AND the v1 boss deals no damage, so the trigger and its rate are both outside the input domain. Guarded live by asserting zero srcSlot 'skill2' damage events.

HP-threshold gates (S2b HP<60%, burst HP<50%) cannot be exercised in the INACTIVE state — the engine models no HP, so the pre-threshold opening ~29s/~38s is unrepresentable. Both are asserted LIVE (dropping them is the failure mode); the over-credit for the opening window is a ⚑ (≈16%/21% of a 180s fight, ~1% of her damage for the crit-damage line) that a rampSec haircut may absorb, and either encoding passes this file.

Shape hedges worth flagging to the judge: the packet describes the OverrideFile slot value BOTH as Block[] and as CharacterSkills{blocks}, so the readers handle both; damage-event attribution prefers unitOf(res,'scarlet').events with a slug-field fallback; and only the documented damage-event fields (bucket/srcSlot/inFullBurst/fbMajorApplied/rangeApplied/mult) are read — no crit/core rate field names are guessed.
